newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae dissident position supported.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae dissident position supported.

text.p: The Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae said Monday two senior Student Loan Marketing Association officers have voiced support for the group's proposals, saying they will vote for the committee's position at the May 9 shareholders meeting.

On Friday, Robert Levine and Mark Overend, respectively the Treasurer and Controller of Sallie Mae, stated in a letter to Sallie Mae's chairman that they believe the committee is in a better position than current Sallie Mae management to ensure that the business opportunities and risks faced by Sallie Mae after privatization are effectively addressed.
The committee, a shareholder group that includes eight current Sallie Mae directors, praised the decision by two senior officers to endorse its proposals and board slate at the special meeting.

Albert L. Lord, a director and committee spokesman, said, "It is important that (shareholders) know the views of these two ... officers at the company. Messrs. Levine and Overend have correctly identified the two important issues that shareholders must evaluate -- leadership capability and responsiveness to the opportunities and risks facing the Company after privatization."

Chief executive "Larry Hough's same old 'business as usual' approach fails on both accounts. Messrs. Levine and Overend are to be commended for holding the interests of shareholders paramount and speaking up on behalf of the capable officers and employees who disagree with Mr. Hough's policies."
The letter from Messrs. Levine and Overend to Sallie Mae Chairman William Arceneaux was attached to the committee's statement. It reads as follows:

"The purpose of this letter is to inform you that, contrary to the implications of certain statements made by the company in connection with its proxy solicitations, Sallie Mae management is not uniformly opposed to the CRV business plan or board slate. We feel an obligation to make you aware of this to assist you in your future deliberations regarding the implementation of any shareholder mandates or further proceedings in conjunction with Sallie Mae's privatization.

"We are concerned that the current corporate culture at Sallie Mae will not be receptive to certain strategic elements of the CRV's business plan which are critical to the future of the company. Like many others, we have remained at Sallie Mae based on a strong belief in the great potential of this franchise. As Sallie Mae privatizes, it is essential to ensure that new approaches to the business are appropriately developed and that the risks facing the Company are properly managed. We believe the CRV is in a better position to ensure these challenges are addressed in an effective manner.

Accordingly, we wish to inform you that, as Sallie Mae shareholders, we intend to cast our votes in favor of the CRV at the special shareholders' meeting on May 9, 1997. As long-time dedicated employees, it is awkward to disagree with Sallie Mae's present leadership. We do so knowing that the first reaction of many will be to retaliate or discount our views, instead of addressing these issues. However, as shareholders and officers, we feel it is our responsibility to state our position."
